title: Treasury and Forex Management
subtitle: Manage a bank's liquidity, interest rate and FX positions in a floating-birr, policy-rate world
summary: Build gap, duration and liquidity analysis, run the FX position within the NBE limit, price customer deals and forwards, and take decisions to a mock ALCO for one Ethiopian bank.
audience: Dealers, ALM analysts, and treasury and finance managers in Ethiopian banks, with basic finance maths and a grounding in banking regulation (Topic 1.a, Level 1, or equivalent).
objectives: Build and interpret gap, duration and liquidity coverage analysis for an Ethiopian bank
Manage the FX position within the NBE limit and price customer FX deals and forwards
Price and classify the investment portfolio within NBE investment limits
Use funds transfer pricing for product pricing and branch profitability
Recommend ALCO strategies for the balance sheet, investment portfolio and funding

runningCase.name: Bank A
runningCase.text: Bank A is a fictional mid-sized Ethiopian private bank with total assets of Birr 120 billion, deposits of Birr 95 billion, loans of Birr 82 billion, Tier 1 capital of Birr 11 billion and paid-up capital of Birr 6 billion. After the credit growth cap was removed, its loans grew faster than deposits, leaving a loan-to-deposit ratio of about 86%, a 30-day funding gap of Birr 5 billion and the risk of a targeted reserve requirement. Import demand has outrun its FX inflows, so its short dollar position keeps growing. Each module adds one part of the analysis, and in Module 5 you present decisions on pricing, investments and funding to a mock ALCO.

modules.title: The ALM framework: repricing gap, earnings and economic value
modules.summary: Measure how a change in the National Bank Rate flows through a bank's earnings and economic value, and read the result the way an ALCO must.
objectives: Explain what asset and liability management covers and how the ALCO uses it
Describe the interest-rate-based monetary framework, the National Bank Rate and its corridor
Build a repricing gap and compute earnings at risk for a rate shock
Estimate the change in economic value of equity from duration
Assess how high inflation and the end of the credit growth cap change ALM decisions

lessons.title: What ALM manages and who decides
body: Asset and liability management (ALM) looks at the whole balance sheet at once. Its job is to keep the bank liquid, protect net interest income from rate moves, keep foreign currency positions within limits and fund growth at a sensible cost. Treasury executes, the middle office measures and the Asset and Liability Committee (ALCO) decides.

The ALCO usually includes the CEO or a deputy, the CFO, the treasurer, the chief risk officer and the heads of credit and retail. It meets at least monthly, more often when markets move. A good ALCO meeting starts with numbers prepared by an independent middle office, not by the dealers whose positions are being judged.
In this course you join the treasury of Bank A, a fictional mid-sized Ethiopian private bank. Each module adds one piece of the analysis, and in Module 5 you write the ALCO paper.

items.label: Decide: ALCO sets prices and limits

regulation.text: The NBE guidelines expect banks to manage credit, liquidity, market and operational risk under board-approved policies, with a risk manager, an ALCO and regular stress testing. They are the baseline for how a treasury and its ALCO are organized.

example.title: Bank A at the start of the year
example.text: Bank A has total assets of Birr 120 billion, deposits of Birr 95 billion and loans of Birr 82 billion, so its loan-to-deposit ratio is about 86%, well above the 72.7% the NBE reported for private banks in July 2026. Its treasurer, Selam Tesfaye, worries about three things: a large funding gap in the next three months, a short dollar position that keeps growing, and the chance that the NBE imposes a targeted reserve requirement because of the high loan-to-deposit ratio.

lessons.tip: Separate the people who take positions from the people who measure them. That single rule prevents most treasury losses.

lessons.title: The rate environment: National Bank Rate, corridor and market rates
body: Since 2024 the NBE runs an interest-rate-based monetary framework. Its Monetary Policy Committee sets the National Bank Rate, and its standing facilities form a corridor around it: banks can deposit surplus funds with the NBE at the lower bound and borrow overnight at the upper bound. At MPC meeting No. 7 on 13 July 2026, the NBE raised the National Bank Rate by 1 point to 16% and kept the corridor at plus or minus 3 points, which puts the standing deposit rate at 13% and the standing lending rate at 19%.

Market rates sit inside or near that corridor. The same release reported a 91-day T-bill yield of 11.0% and a 7-day interbank rate of 14.6%, with headline inflation of 13.4% in May 2026. These numbers change at every MPC meeting, so treasury must refresh them before each ALCO.

Since January 2026 banks set their own deposit and lending rates. A change in the National Bank Rate does not force a change in customer rates, but competitors and funding costs usually move with it, so the ALCO has to decide how fast to follow.

visual.caption: Rates reported in or implied by the MPC No. 7 release (July 2026). Update before use.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest rates (as amended)
regulation.text: Each bank sets its deposit and lending rates freely, with no minimum deposit rate. Rates must be approved in writing by the board on explicit written criteria, changes reported to the NBE within 5 working days and monthly weighted average rates within 7 working days. The NBE sets the rates on its own lending and standing facilities; interbank rates are negotiated between banks.

scenario.title: The MPC raises the rate
scenario.situation: The MPC raises the National Bank Rate by 1 point. Bank A's competitors announce higher time deposit rates the next week. Bank A's loans reprice only at each review date, while most of its savings and time deposits can be repriced within three months.
scenario.question: What should Selam recommend to the ALCO first?
options: Raise all deposit rates by 1 point immediately to match competitors
Measure the repricing gap and earnings at risk, then propose deposit and loan rate changes the board can approve on written criteria
Keep all rates unchanged because the directive no longer sets a minimum deposit rate
Ask the NBE which customer rates to set
scenario.explain: Rates are now a board decision based on written criteria, so the ALCO needs the measured impact before it reprices. Matching competitors blindly can cut margins, ignoring them can lose deposits, and the NBE no longer sets customer rates.

lessons.title: Building the repricing gap
body: A repricing gap sorts rate-sensitive assets (RSA) and rate-sensitive liabilities (RSL) into time buckets by the date their rate can next change, not by their final maturity. A five-year loan whose rate the bank can revise every quarter sits in the 0 to 3 month bucket.

The gap in each bucket is RSA minus RSL. A negative gap means the bank is liability sensitive: when rates rise, its funding costs reset before its asset yields. A positive gap means it is asset sensitive. Savings deposits have no contractual repricing date, so the ALCO must agree a behavioral assumption about how much reprices when the policy rate moves.

visual.caption: Computed bucket by bucket; the running total is the cumulative gap.

worked.title: Bank A repricing gap within one year (Birr billions)

rows.label: 0 to 3 months RSA: loans 20, T-bills 6, interbank placements 2
0 to 3 months RSL: savings assumed to reprice 30, time deposits 12, borrowings 3

worked.note: Bank A is liability sensitive in the short bucket: a rate rise lifts its funding costs before its loan yields.

example.title: The savings assumption that changed the picture
example.text: Dawit Alemu, Bank A's ALM analyst, first placed all Birr 48 billion of savings deposits in the 0 to 3 month bucket, which made the short gap minus 35 billion. Reviewing two years of rate changes, he found that the bank had passed on rate changes to only about 30 billion of savings balances, mainly large urban accounts. The ALCO approved the 30 billion assumption, documented the evidence and agreed to review it every six months.

lessons.title: Earnings at risk
body: Earnings at risk (EaR) estimates the change in net interest income over the next 12 months for a given rate shock. For each bucket, multiply the gap by the rate change and by the part of the year left after the bucket reprices, usually measured from the bucket midpoint.

EaR is a short-term, accounting view. It answers the question the board asks first: how much will this year's income move? It does not capture what happens to positions repricing after one year, which is why the ALCO also looks at economic value.
points: Change in NII = gap x rate change x (12 minus midpoint month) / 12
Use the same shock for assets and liabilities only as a starting point; then test a case where deposits reprice faster
Express the result in Birr and as a share of budgeted NII

worked.title: Bank A earnings at risk for a 2 point rise (Birr billions)

rows.label: Change as a share of NII

worked.note: A 2 point rise would cut about Birr 245 million from next year's net interest income, before any repricing action.

scenario.title: Reading an EaR limit
scenario.situation: Bank A's board has set an EaR limit of 5% of budgeted NII for a 2 point shock. The measured figure is 4.7%. The retail team plans a campaign that would add Birr 6 billion of 3-month time deposits funding fixed-rate 2-year loans.
scenario.question: What is the best advice to the ALCO?
options: Approve: the bank is inside its limit today
Approve only if the loans are to government enterprises
Re-run EaR with the campaign included, since adding short liabilities against longer fixed assets widens the negative gap and may breach the limit
scenario.explain: Limits apply to the position after the decision, not before it. The campaign adds short liabilities against longer fixed assets, so the gap widens and the EaR could exceed 5%.

lessons.title: Economic value of equity and duration
body: Economic value of equity (EVE) is the present value of assets minus the present value of liabilities. When rates rise, the value of fixed-rate assets falls; if assets have a longer duration than liabilities, equity value falls too.

Modified duration gives a quick estimate: the percentage change in value is about minus modified duration times the change in yield. Applied to both sides of the balance sheet, the change in EVE is about minus (asset duration x assets minus liability duration x liabilities) x change in yield.

left.title: Earnings at risk
items: Horizon: next 12 months
Measures: change in net interest income
Captures: repricing within the year
Audience: budget and profit planning

right.title: Economic value of equity
items: Horizon: life of all positions
Measures: change in present value of equity
Captures: long fixed-rate assets and liabilities
Audience: capital and long-term strategy

worked.title: Bank A change in EVE for a 2 point rise (Birr billions)

rows.label: Change as a share of equity

worked.note: Both views point the same way: Bank A loses when rates rise. The EVE result is large because of fixed-rate loans and bonds held for several years.

example.title: Long bonds in a rising rate cycle
example.text: A bank in Hawassa had bought several years of fixed-rate government bonds when yields were lower. When market rates rose, the bonds lost value while its deposits repriced upward. Its income statement looked fine because the bonds were at amortised cost, but its economic value had fallen and the bonds could not be sold for liquidity without a loss. The ALCO later set a duration limit on the investment book.

lessons.title: Inflation, real rates and the end of the credit growth cap
body: Inflation of 13.4% (May 2026) means that a time deposit paying 12% gives the customer a negative real return. Depositors move to banks that pay more or to real assets, so deposit pricing becomes a competitive and liquidity question, not only a margin question.

At MPC No. 7 the NBE removed the temporary credit growth cap and introduced a targeted, additional reserve requirement that it may impose on individual banks based on their loan-to-deposit ratio. Banks may now grow loans faster, but a bank that lends far ahead of its deposits risks extra reserves, which tie up funds at no return and widen the funding gap.
For ALM this means loan growth plans and deposit mobilization targets must be set together, with the loan-to-deposit ratio as a key ALCO indicator.

regulation.source: NBE Monetary Policy Committee, meeting No. 7 (13 July 2026)
regulation.text: The NBE raised the National Bank Rate to 16% with a corridor of plus or minus 3 points, removed the credit growth cap, introduced a targeted (additional) reserve requirement linked to each bank's loan-to-deposit ratio, cut the NBE FX commission from 2.5% to 1.5% and cut the surrender requirement on goods exports from 50% to 30%.

scenario.title: Growth after the cap
scenario.situation: With the credit growth cap removed, Bank A's business units ask for Birr 15 billion of new loans next year. Deposits are budgeted to grow by Birr 8 billion. The loan-to-deposit ratio is already about 86%, against 72.7% for private banks as a group.
scenario.question: What should the ALCO do?
options: Approve the full Birr 15 billion because the cap is gone
Freeze all new lending until the ratio falls below the sector figure
Fund the extra loans from the NBE standing lending facility
Set loan growth in line with funded deposit growth and the liquidity plan, and tie any extra lending to new deposit or term funding
scenario.explain: Removing the cap does not remove the funding constraint, and a rising ratio raises the risk of a targeted reserve requirement. A freeze is unnecessary, and the standing facility is an overnight backstop, not a source of term funding.

example.title: Real rates and the depositor
example.text: Almaz Haile keeps Birr 2 million in a one-year time deposit at 12%. With inflation at 13.4%, her money loses about 1.4% of purchasing power a year. When a competitor offers 14%, she moves. Multiply her by thousands of customers and the bank's deposit outflow assumption must change.

lessons.tip: Put the loan-to-deposit ratio on the first page of every ALCO pack, next to the latest sector figure from the MPC release.

takeaways: ALM manages liquidity, interest rate and FX risk together; the ALCO decides on numbers from an independent middle office.
The National Bank Rate (16% since July 2026) and its plus or minus 3 point corridor anchor Birr market rates, but banks set customer rates freely on board-approved criteria.
A repricing gap sorts positions by repricing date; a negative short gap means rising rates cut income.
Earnings at risk shows the 12-month income effect; economic value of equity shows the long-run value effect.
With the credit cap removed, loan growth must be matched with funding to avoid a targeted reserve requirement.

quiz.q: A five-year loan whose rate the bank may revise every quarter belongs in which repricing bucket?
quiz.explain: Repricing gap uses the next repricing date, not the final maturity.

quiz.q: Bank A's 0 to 3 month gap is minus Birr 17 billion. What happens to its income if rates rise?
options: It falls, because liabilities reprice before assets
It rises, because assets reprice first
It depends only on the 3 to 12 month bucket
quiz.explain: A negative gap means liabilities reset first, so a rise in rates raises costs faster than yields.

quiz.q: With the National Bank Rate at 16% and a corridor of plus or minus 3 points, where is the standing lending facility rate?
quiz.explain: The upper bound of the corridor is 16% plus 3 points, or 19%.

quiz.q: Under NBE/INT/13/2026, who sets a bank's savings deposit rate?
options: The NBE, through a minimum rate
The bank, with written board approval on explicit criteria
quiz.explain: Banks set deposit and lending rates freely on board-approved written criteria and report them to the NBE.

quiz.q: Assets of Birr 100 billion have modified duration 1.5 and liabilities of Birr 90 billion have modified duration 0.5. Roughly how much does EVE change for a 1 point rise?
quiz.explain: Minus (1.5 x 100 minus 0.5 x 90) x 1% = minus (150 minus 45) x 1% = minus Birr 1.05 billion.

quiz.q: Why does the end of the credit growth cap not mean unlimited loan growth for a bank with a high loan-to-deposit ratio?
options: The cap still applies to private banks
The NBE may impose a targeted reserve requirement based on the loan-to-deposit ratio, and funding must still be found
The NBE sets each bank's loan budget
quiz.explain: MPC No. 7 replaced the cap with a targeted reserve requirement linked to the loan-to-deposit ratio.

modules.title: Liquidity risk management
modules.summary: Forecast cash flows, set behavioral assumptions, stress the balance sheet and prepare a contingency funding plan that works in Ethiopian markets.
objectives: Map the Birr liquidity sources available to an Ethiopian bank, from deposits to NBE facilities
Build a maturity ladder and identify the funding gap
Set and defend behavioral assumptions for deposits and loan drawdowns
Run a liquidity stress test and compute an LCR and NSFR on a course basis
Design a contingency funding plan with triggers and actions

lessons.title: Where Birr liquidity comes from
body: An Ethiopian bank's liquidity rests on customer deposits, its holdings of T-bills and other government securities, the interbank money market and the NBE's facilities. T-bills are issued at auctions with tenors from 28 to 364 days and can be sold or used as collateral when the bank needs cash.

The NBE Proclamation gives the NBE a set of monetary instruments, including credit operations, open market operations, its own short-term debt, a standing deposit facility, overnight lending and intraday facilities, and minimum reserves. As lender of last resort the NBE may lend to a bank in difficulty, at a rate above the policy rate. Treasury should treat the NBE as a backstop, not a funding plan.

items.label: Customer deposits
items.text: The core funding base: savings, demand and time deposits.

items.label: T-bills
items.text: 28 to 364 days; sell or repo for cash.

items.label: Interbank market
items.text: Borrow from or lend to other banks at negotiated rates.

items.label: NBE standing facilities
items.text: Overnight deposit and lending at the corridor bounds.

items.label: Intraday facility
items.text: Covers payment timing within the day.

items.label: Lender of last resort
items.text: Emergency lending above the policy rate.

regulation.source: National Bank of Ethiopia Proclamation No. 1359/2025, Articles 29 and 30
regulation.text: Article 29 lists the NBE's monetary instruments: credit operations, open market operations, NBE short-term debt, a standing deposit facility, overnight lending and intraday facilities, and minimum reserves. Article 30 makes the NBE lender of last resort, lending at a rate above the policy rate.

example.title: A Friday payment crunch
example.text: On a Friday afternoon Bank A must settle a Birr 1.2 billion customer transfer through the payment system, but expected interbank receipts arrive late. The treasury desk uses the NBE intraday facility to settle on time and repays it when the funds come in, avoiding an overnight borrowing at the 19% standing lending rate.

lessons.title: The maturity ladder and the funding gap
body: A maturity ladder lists expected cash inflows and outflows by time band: overnight, up to 7 days, up to 30 days, 1 to 3 months and so on. The net flow in each band, and its running total, shows when the bank will run short and by how much.

Unlike the repricing gap, the ladder looks at cash, not rates. A loan that reprices quarterly but matures in five years brings in only its installments in the next month. Time deposits are shown at contract maturity, then adjusted by the expected rollover rate.

items.label: Overnight
items.text: Payment flows, NBE settlement balance

items.label: Up to 7 days
items.text: Interbank maturities, T-bill auction settlement

items.label: 8 to 30 days
items.text: Time deposit maturities, loan disbursements

items.label: 1 to 3 months
items.text: Larger T-bill maturities, seasonal outflows

items.label: 3 to 12 months
items.text: Structural gap, funding plan horizon

worked.title: Bank A 30-day maturity ladder, base case (Birr billions)

rows.label: Outflows: savings and demand deposit run-off (behavioral)
Outflows: time deposits not rolled over

worked.note: Bank A needs Birr 5 billion within a month, even before any stress. It has T-bills it can sell or repo, but the gap must be planned, not discovered.

lessons.title: Behavioral assumptions: core and volatile deposits
body: Demand and savings deposits can be withdrawn at any time, yet most stay for years. ALM splits them into a core part, which behaves like long-term funding, and a volatile part that can leave quickly. Time deposits are judged by their rollover rate, and committed credit lines by how much customers draw.

Assumptions must come from the bank's own data: daily balances over several years, behavior around holidays, rate changes and news, and concentration in large depositors. Large institutional and government deposits deserve their own assumption, because one decision by one treasurer can move billions.
points: Core share of savings: the lowest balance held over a long period, adjusted for growth
Rollover rate of time deposits: measured per segment and per tenor
Concentration: top 20 depositors as a share of deposits
Seasonality: fiscal year end, holidays, coffee harvest and payment cycles

example.title: The institutional deposit that left
example.text: A public enterprise held Birr 3 billion in demand deposits at Bank A, treated as 80% core. At its fiscal year end it moved Birr 2.5 billion to pay suppliers through another bank. The ALCO reclassified large institutional deposits as volatile and set a concentration limit for the top 20 depositors.

scenario.title: Simulation round: remittance inflow and an import payment
scenario.situation: In one morning Bank A receives diaspora remittances of USD 4 million that customers convert to Birr, and Adama Steel Works PLC asks to buy USD 6 million for an import payment due in three days. Interbank Birr is available at about 14.6%.
scenario.question: How should treasury handle the day's liquidity?
options: Record both on the maturity ladder: the remittance conversion adds FX bought and Birr paid out, the import sale brings Birr in and FX out; fund any Birr gap overnight or by T-bill repo
Ignore the import payment until the settlement day
Refuse the import request to protect liquidity
Treat the remittance inflow as core funding for five-year loans
scenario.explain: Both deals move Birr and FX on known dates, so they belong in the ladder now. Refusing a customer is a last resort, and remittance conversions are one-off flows, not core deposits.

lessons.title: Liquidity stress testing
body: A stress test asks what happens if the assumptions fail. A bank-specific scenario might be a rumor that triggers deposit withdrawals; a market scenario might be a tight interbank market after a large T-bill auction; a combined scenario has both.

The key result is the survival horizon: how many days the bank can meet stressed outflows from its liquid assets without new funding. The ALCO sets a minimum horizon and the actions to take before it is reached.

items.label: Choose scenarios
items.text: Bank-specific, market-wide and combined

items.label: Set stressed run-off rates
items.text: By deposit segment and funding source

items.label: Value liquid assets
items.text: After haircuts for sale or repo

items.label: Compute survival horizon
items.text: Days until liquid assets run out

items.label: Agree actions
items.text: Link results to the contingency plan

scenario.title: A rumor on social media
scenario.situation: A false message claims Bank A has liquidity problems. Withdrawals in two days are three times normal. The stress test shows a survival horizon of about 28 days, against an ALCO minimum of 30.
scenario.question: What is the best first response?
options: Wait for withdrawals to stop on their own
Activate the contingency funding plan: raise liquidity by T-bill repo or sale, slow new disbursements, inform the NBE and communicate calmly to customers
Raise all deposit rates by 5 points overnight
Borrow from the NBE lender of last resort facility immediately
scenario.explain: The plan exists for this moment. Market funding and asset sales come first; a sudden rate jump signals panic, and lender of last resort support is for when market options are exhausted.

lessons.title: LCR and NSFR as concepts
body: The Basel III liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) compares high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) with net cash outflows over 30 stressed days; the standard expects HQLA at least to cover those outflows. The net stable funding ratio (NSFR) compares available stable funding with required stable funding over one year.

These are international concepts. Ethiopian banks report against the NBE's liquidity requirement, so treat the LCR and NSFR as internal management tools until the NBE adopts them. The run-off and funding factors below are illustrative for this course.

visual.caption: A ratio of 1.0 or more means liquid assets cover a month of stressed outflows.

worked.title: Bank A LCR on a course basis (Birr billions)

rows.label: HQLA: cash and excess NBE balance 3.0, T-bills 10.0
Outflow: less stable retail deposits 25 x 10%
Outflow: corporate and institutional deposits 30 x 30%
Inflows: loan installments 2.5 x 50% plus placements 2.0
NSFR on the same basis (stable funding 87.5 / required 83.15)

worked.note: Bank A's structural funding is adequate, but its short-term buffer falls just short of a month of stress, largely because of concentrated corporate deposits.

regulation.source: NBE liquidity requirement directive (number to confirm)
regulation.text: Banks must hold a minimum ratio of liquid assets to liabilities set by the NBE, alongside minimum reserves held at the NBE. Check the current directive for the ratio and the eligible assets before setting internal limits; internal triggers should sit above the regulatory floor.

lessons.title: The contingency funding plan
body: A contingency funding plan (CFP) sets out early warning indicators, the stages of a liquidity event, who decides, and the actions in order of cost. It is approved by the board and tested at least once a year.

Actions are ranked from cheapest and least visible to most expensive: use surplus interbank lines, repo T-bills, slow new loan commitments, sell securities, raise term deposits, and finally use NBE standing lending at the top of the corridor or ask for lender of last resort support.
points: Early warnings: deposit outflows above a set percentage, rising interbank cost, fewer counterparties willing to lend, negative news
Roles: treasurer leads, CRO monitors, CEO chairs the crisis team, communications prepares messages
Test: a desk exercise each year using a realistic Ethiopian scenario

example.title: Testing the plan before it is needed
example.text: Bank A ran a CFP drill based on a scenario of a large public enterprise withdrawal combined with a tight interbank market after a big T-bill auction. The drill found that two interbank counterparties had cut their lines without telling treasury, and that the repo documentation for T-bills was not ready. Both were fixed within a month.

scenario.title: Ranking funding actions
scenario.situation: Bank A needs Birr 5 billion for the next month. Options: repo T-bills at about the interbank rate, raise 6-month term deposits at 15%, or borrow overnight from the NBE at the 19% standing lending rate and roll it daily.
scenario.question: Which order of actions fits a sound CFP?
options: NBE standing lending first, then repo, then term deposits
Repo T-bills for the immediate gap, raise term deposits to close it structurally, keep NBE standing lending as the backstop
Raise term deposits only, at any rate
scenario.explain: Repo is quick and cheap, term deposits fix the structure, and the standing facility is the most expensive overnight backstop. Selling all T-bills leaves no buffer.

takeaways: Deposits, T-bills, the interbank market and NBE facilities are the Birr liquidity sources; the NBE is a backstop, not a funding plan.
A maturity ladder shows when and by how much the bank runs short; Bank A faces a Birr 5 billion 30-day gap in its base case.
Behavioral assumptions must come from the bank's own data, with large institutional deposits treated separately.
Stress tests give a survival horizon that the ALCO compares with a minimum and links to the contingency funding plan.
LCR and NSFR are useful internal tools; regulatory compliance is measured against the NBE liquidity requirement.

quiz.q: Which NBE facility is designed to cover payment timing within a single day?
quiz.explain: Proclamation No. 1359/2025 lists intraday facilities among the NBE's instruments.

quiz.q: Under Article 30 of Proclamation No. 1359/2025, at what rate does the NBE lend as lender of last resort?
options: At a rate above the policy rate
quiz.explain: Emergency lending is priced above the policy rate to discourage reliance on it.

quiz.q: A maturity ladder differs from a repricing gap because it:
options: Shows cash flows by when they occur
quiz.explain: The ladder is about cash timing; the repricing gap is about rate resets.

quiz.q: HQLA are Birr 9 billion and net 30-day stressed outflows are Birr 12 billion. What is the LCR?
Which deposit source most needs its own behavioral assumption?
options: A few large institutional and government deposits
quiz.explain: Concentrated balances can leave on one decision, so they are volatile even when they look stable.

quiz.q: In a contingency funding plan, where does NBE standing lending usually sit?
options: Near the end, as the costly backstop
First action, because it is easiest
quiz.explain: At the top of the corridor it is the most expensive routine source and signals stress.

modules.title: FX risk, dealing and forwards
modules.summary: Run the bank's foreign currency position within the NBE limit, price customer deals and forwards, and control the dealing room.
objectives: Explain how the market-based FX regime works since July 2024 and what has changed since
Quote spot and cross rates and price customer FX deals
Compute the net open position and test it against the NBE limit
Estimate value at risk and explain the market risk capital link
Price a forward contract and apply dealing room controls

lessons.title: The FX regime since July 2024
body: FXD/01/2024, in force since 29 July 2024, lets banks buy and sell foreign currency with customers and with each other at freely negotiated rates. The NBE publishes a non-binding Indicative Daily Exchange Rate, and an interbank market has developed alongside client dealing.

Exporters of goods originally converted 50% of proceeds and kept 50% in retention accounts; MPC No. 7 in July 2026 cut the surrender requirement on goods exports to 30%. Under FXD/04/2026, service exporters may keep 100% of proceeds. Banks also hand the NBE foreign cash notes above 10% of their paid-up capital, and the NBE commission on FX transactions was cut from 2.5% to 1.5% in July 2026.
For treasury, this means FX is now a priced market. The bank buys from exporters and remitters, sells to importers, and carries a position in between that it must manage.

items.label: July 2024
items.text: FXD/01/2024: freely negotiated rates, interbank market, indicative rate

items.label: February 2026
items.text: FXD/04/2026: forward contracts, 100% retention for service exporters

items.label: May 2026
items.text: FXD/05/2026: banks approve LCs on acceptance for FX account holders

items.label: July 2026
items.text: MPC No. 7: goods export surrender cut to 30%, NBE FX commission to 1.5%

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/01/2024, Foreign exchange (as amended by FXD/04/2026)
regulation.text: Banks deal with clients and each other at freely negotiated rates; the NBE publishes an indicative daily rate that is not binding. Exporters must repatriate proceeds within 90 days. FXD/04/2026 adds forward contracts, lets service exporters retain 100% of proceeds, and lets banks approve dividend remittances and external loans with monthly reporting to the NBE.

example.title: Where Bank A's dollars come from and go
example.text: In a typical week Bank A buys about USD 9 million: from coffee exporter Sidama Coffee Exporters PLC, from diaspora remittances and from NGOs converting grants. It sells about USD 11 million to importers such as Mekelle Pharma Importers PLC and Adama Steel Works PLC. The USD 2 million weekly difference is why its short dollar position keeps growing.

lessons.title: Quotes, spreads and cross rates
body: A Birr quote gives a bid (the rate at which the bank buys foreign currency) and an ask (the rate at which it sells). The spread between them pays for the dealer's risk and costs. The NBE indicative rate is a reference, not a price the bank must use.

For currencies with thin Birr trading, such as the euro, banks derive a cross rate from USD/ETB and EUR/USD. To find the rate at which the bank sells euros for Birr, multiply the two ask rates; to find its buying rate, multiply the two bid rates. Rates in this course are illustrative.

worked.title: Deriving a EUR/ETB quote (illustrative rates)

rows.label: Cost to an importer buying EUR 500,000 at the ask

worked.note: Using the bid for one leg and the ask for the other would misprice the deal and give away the spread.

scenario.title: Pricing a large import
scenario.situation: Mekelle Pharma Importers PLC wants to buy USD 3 million today. The screen shows interbank USD/ETB at 151.20 / 151.80. Bank A is already short dollars and close to its position limit.
scenario.question: How should the dealer price the deal?
options: At the NBE indicative rate, because it is official
At the interbank bid, to win the customer
Refuse, because the bank is short
At a rate above the interbank ask that covers the cost of buying the dollars back and the position risk, quoted clearly to the customer
scenario.explain: The bank sells at its ask, which must cover the cost of covering the position in the market. The indicative rate is non-binding, and refusing a good customer is unnecessary if the deal is priced and covered.

lessons.title: The net open position and the NBE limit
body: The net open position (NOP) is the bank's exposure to exchange rate moves. For each currency, it is FX assets minus FX liabilities, plus forward purchases minus forward sales. A long position gains when the foreign currency strengthens; a short position loses.

Under SBB/96/2025 the overall open position may not exceed plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 capital at the close of each business day. Banks set their own single-currency limits within that cap, must square any excess by the next business day and report daily. A common method for the overall position, the shorthand method, takes the larger of total longs and total shorts in Birr; confirm the method against the NBE reporting template.

visual.caption: Convert each currency to Birr at the mid rate, then compare the overall position with 18% of Tier 1.

worked.title: Bank A overall open position at close (Birr millions)

rows.label: Position as a share of Tier 1
Excess to square by next business day

worked.note: Bank A is in breach. It must buy about USD 1.6 million or more, or reduce dollar liabilities, by the next business day and report the breach.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/96/2025, Foreign exchange exposure limits of banks
regulation.text: In force from 10 November 2025: a bank's overall open foreign currency position may not exceed plus or minus 18% of its Tier 1 capital at the close of each business day. Banks set single-currency limits within that cap, square any excess by the next business day and report daily. Breaches and late or false reporting carry fines. It repeals SBB/27/2001.

scenario.title: Closing the breach
scenario.situation: It is 4 p.m. and Bank A's overall position is 20.1% of Tier 1, short dollars. Hirut Bekele, the chief dealer, says the birr will probably weaken further next week, so buying dollars now is right anyway, but the interbank ask is high today.
scenario.question: What should treasury do?
options: Wait until next week for a better rate
Reclassify some dollar deposits as Birr in the report
Ask a customer to delay an import payment to after the reporting date
Buy enough dollars in the interbank market, or agree forward purchases, to bring the position within 18% by the next business day, and report the breach
scenario.explain: The directive requires the excess to be squared by the next business day and reported. Misreporting or manipulating customer timing breaks both the rule and the code of conduct.

lessons.title: Value at risk and the capital link
body: Value at risk (VaR) estimates the loss that should not be exceeded on a given share of days. A simple parametric VaR is position x daily volatility x a confidence factor (about 1.65 for 95%). For a longer horizon, multiply by the square root of the number of days.

VaR depends on history. After a regime change like July 2024, past volatility may understate risk, so treasury should add stress scenarios such as a sudden 10% move. Under SBB/95/2025 banks also hold capital for market risk using a simplified Basel III approach, so a larger FX position consumes capital that could support lending.

worked.title: Bank A dollar position VaR (illustrative volatility)

rows.label: Ten-day VaR: 21.0 x square root of 10
Stress: 10% move on the full position

worked.note: The stress loss is three times the ten-day VaR. The ALCO should see both.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/95/2025, Risk-based capital adequacy
regulation.text: Banks must hold CET1 of at least 7%, Tier 1 of at least 9% and total capital of at least 11% of risk-weighted assets, which include a simplified Basel III market risk charge and a standardized operational risk charge. The directive is in force from 10 November 2025, with quarterly reporting from Q1 2026 and full compliance by 31 December 2026.

example.title: When history understated the risk
example.text: Before July 2024 the official rate moved by small steps, so a VaR model based on that history showed tiny daily volatility. A bank that used it to set dealer limits after the float found that one week's market move exceeded its 'one-in-twenty' daily loss estimate many times over. It rebuilt the model on post-float data and added fixed stress scenarios.

lessons.title: Forward contracts under FXD/04/2026
body: FXD/04/2026 allows banks to offer forward rates. The directive text sets no tenor or eligibility limits, so each bank's policy and the FX market code must set them. A forward lets an importer fix today the Birr cost of a payment due in three months, and lets an exporter fix the Birr value of future receipts.

The fair forward rate comes from interest rate parity: the bank can borrow Birr, buy dollars spot and place them until the delivery date. The forward rate is spot x (1 + Birr rate x days / 365) / (1 + USD rate x days / 365). With Birr rates higher than dollar rates, the forward rate is above spot.

worked.title: Three-month USD/ETB forward (illustrative rates)
worked.note: The customer quote adds the bank's spread and credit charge to this mid rate.

scenario.title: A forward for a steel importer
scenario.situation: Adama Steel Works PLC must pay USD 2 million in 90 days and asks Bank A for a forward. Its credit line is fully used, and its finance manager, Tewodros Abebe, says it may cancel the order if steel prices fall.
scenario.question: What should Bank A require before dealing?
options: Nothing: forwards carry no credit risk
A pre-settlement credit limit or margin for the forward, documentation of the underlying import, and clear terms for early close-out
Payment of the full Birr amount today
scenario.explain: If the customer walks away, the bank must close the forward at the market rate, which is a credit exposure. A limit, documents and close-out terms control it; asking for full payment today defeats the purpose of a forward.

lessons.tip: Treat every forward as a loan for the size of the possible rate move: it needs a credit limit.

lessons.title: Dealing room conduct and controls
body: Every deal follows the same path: captured in the system at once by the dealer, confirmed with the counterparty by the back office, settled through SWIFT and the nostro account, and reconciled. The middle office checks limits and revalues positions daily.

FXD/01/2024 refers to an FX Market Operation Guideline and Code of Conduct for the interbank market. Whatever its final text, the core rules are universal: deal at market rates, never off-market to hide a loss or favor a customer, record all calls, respect dealer limits and report errors at once.

items.label: Deal capture
items.text: Dealer enters the deal immediately

items.label: Limit check
items.text: Middle office checks dealer, counterparty and position limits

items.label: Confirmation
items.text: Back office confirms terms with the counterparty

items.label: Settlement
items.text: Payment by SWIFT through the nostro account

items.label: Reconciliation
items.text: Nostro statement matched to the books daily

example.title: A nostro break found in time
example.text: Bank A's back office found a USD 250,000 difference between its books and the nostro statement from its correspondent. The cause was a deal captured twice by a dealer and confirmed only once. Because reconciliation ran daily, the error was corrected the next morning, before it distorted the open position report.

scenario.title: An off-market request
scenario.situation: A large customer asks a dealer to book a dollar sale at yesterday's lower rate because 'the price was agreed by phone'. There is no recorded call or captured deal from yesterday.
scenario.question: What should the dealer do?
options: Book it at yesterday's rate to keep the customer happy
Book it and correct it later
Book it at today's market rate, or escalate to the chief dealer; never book an off-market rate without a recorded deal
scenario.explain: An off-market rate without evidence transfers value from the bank and breaks the code of conduct. Recorded lines and immediate capture exist to settle exactly this kind of dispute.

takeaways: Since July 2024 the Birr trades at freely negotiated rates; the NBE indicative rate is a reference, not a price.
Cross rates use bid times bid and ask times ask; mixing them gives away the spread.
SBB/96/2025 caps the overall open position at plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 capital at each close, with excess squared by the next business day.
VaR built on pre-float history understates risk; add stress scenarios and remember the market risk capital charge under SBB/95/2025.
Forwards, allowed by FXD/04/2026, are priced from interest rate parity and need credit limits and documentation.

quiz.q: Under SBB/96/2025, Bank A's Tier 1 capital is Birr 11 billion. What is the maximum overall open position?
quiz.explain: 18% x Birr 11 billion = Birr 1.98 billion.

quiz.q: USD/ETB is 150.00 / 153.00 and EUR/USD is 1.0800 / 1.0820. At what rate does the bank sell euros for Birr?
quiz.explain: The bank's selling rate is ask times ask: 153.00 x 1.0820 = 165.55.

quiz.q: A bank holds foreign cash notes worth more than 10% of its paid-up capital. What does FXD/01/2024 require?
options: Hand the excess to the NBE
Sell the notes to forex bureaus
quiz.explain: Banks hand the NBE cash notes above 10% of paid-up capital.

quiz.q: Spot is 100, the Birr rate is 16% and the USD rate is 4%, for one year. What is the forward rate, roughly?
Why can a VaR model based on pre-July 2024 data understate FX risk?
options: The administered rate moved little, so historical volatility was far lower than after the float
The data were in a different currency
quiz.explain: Regime change makes past volatility a poor guide, so stress tests are needed.

quiz.q: Which control most directly stops a dealer hiding a loss with an off-market rate?
options: Independent confirmation and daily revaluation by the middle office
quiz.explain: Independent confirmation and market revaluation expose deals booked away from market rates.

modules.title: Investment portfolio and funds transfer pricing
modules.summary: Price and classify the bank's securities within NBE limits, and use funds transfer pricing to price products and measure branch profitability.
objectives: Describe the instruments in an Ethiopian bank's investment portfolio and their role
Price a T-bill and convert between discount and yield
Classify securities under IFRS 9 and explain the ALM consequences
Apply the SBB/92/2024 investment limits to a proposed investment
Build a matched-maturity FTP rate and use it for pricing and branch results

lessons.title: What the investment portfolio is for
body: A bank's securities portfolio does three jobs: it is the liquidity buffer, a source of income when loan demand is weak or risky, and collateral for repo with the NBE or other banks. In Ethiopia the main instruments are T-bills, longer government bonds, NBE instruments used in open market operations, and a small but growing set of corporate bonds, with the Ethiopian Securities Exchange fixed income market adding a trading venue.

Under SBB/95/2025, Birr exposures to the Ethiopian sovereign carry a 0% risk weight, so T-bills use no credit risk capital. They still carry interest rate risk: a long bond bought at a low yield loses value when rates rise, as Module 1 showed.

items.label: T-bills
items.text: 28 to 364 days, sold at a discount at auction

items.label: Government bonds
items.text: Longer tenor, higher duration

items.label: NBE instruments
items.text: Short-term NBE debt and repo in open market operations

items.label: Corporate bonds
items.text: Credit risk on top of rate risk

items.label: Equity stakes
items.text: Limited by SBB/92/2024

example.title: Bank A's portfolio mix
example.text: Bank A holds Birr 10 billion of T-bills and Birr 5 billion of other government and legacy bonds, including bonds bought under the repealed requirement to invest in development bonds. The T-bills are its main liquidity buffer; the legacy bonds are long, low-yielding and cannot easily be sold, so Dawit treats them as illiquid in the stress test.

lessons.title: T-bill maths: price, discount and yield
body: T-bills pay their face value at maturity and are bought at a discount. For a given yield, price = face value / (1 + yield x days / 365). The discount rate is a different measure: (face value minus price) / face value x 365 / days. The discount rate is always lower than the yield on the same bill, so compare like with like.
Day count conventions matter. This course uses actual days over 365; check the Ministry of Finance auction notice for the convention and the auction calendar before bidding.

worked.title: Pricing a 91-day T-bill at an 11.0% yield (per Birr 100 face)

rows.label: Cost of Birr 1 billion face value

worked.note: A bid stated as a discount rate of 11% would give a lower price (97.26) and a higher yield than 11%: always state which measure a bid uses.

scenario.title: Bidding at the T-bill auction
scenario.situation: The 7-day interbank rate is 14.6%, the last 91-day auction cleared at 11.0% and Bank A has a Birr 5 billion 30-day funding gap. The treasurer is asked to bid for Birr 3 billion of 364-day bills.
scenario.question: What is the best advice?
options: Bid for the full amount: T-bills carry no risk
Bid only within the liquidity plan; with a funding gap and interbank funding above the T-bill yield, buying long bills funded overnight loses money and adds duration
Borrow from the NBE standing facility to buy the bills
Sell all existing T-bills and buy the 364-day bills
scenario.explain: Funding at about 14.6% to earn around 11% has negative carry, and a 364-day bill adds rate risk while the bank is short of cash. Zero credit risk does not mean zero risk.

lessons.title: Accounting classification under IFRS 9
body: Under IFRS 9 a debt security is measured at amortised cost if it is held to collect contractual cash flows of principal and interest, at fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI) if held both to collect and to sell, and at fair value through profit or loss otherwise.

The choice shapes ALM. Amortised cost hides price swings from profit, but selling such bonds often can call the business model into question. FVOCI shows value changes in equity, which makes rate risk visible and keeps the bonds available for liquidity.

left.title: Amortised cost
items: Business model: hold to collect
Price changes do not hit profit or equity
Frequent sales undermine the classification
Suits long bonds held to maturity

right.title: Fair value through OCI
items: Business model: hold to collect and sell
Price changes go to equity reserves
Can be sold for liquidity
Suits the liquidity buffer

example.title: The bonds that could not be sold
example.text: A bank classified all its government bonds at amortised cost. In a liquidity squeeze it needed to sell some, but auditors warned that large sales would force a review of the whole portfolio's classification. The ALCO then split the book: a liquidity portfolio at FVOCI and a hold-to-collect portfolio at amortised cost.

scenario.title: Classifying the liquidity buffer
scenario.situation: Bank A plans to hold Birr 4 billion of T-bills and short bonds as its stress buffer, ready to sell or repo whenever needed. The finance team prefers amortised cost to keep profit stable.
scenario.question: Which classification fits the purpose?
options: Fair value through OCI, because the business model is to collect and sell when liquidity requires
Amortised cost, because profit is more stable
Fair value through profit or loss, to maximize trading income
No classification is needed for T-bills
scenario.explain: The classification follows the business model. A buffer that will be sold when needed is held to collect and sell, which points to FVOCI.

lessons.title: Investment limits under SBB/92/2024
body: SBB/92/2024 limits how much of its capital a bank can put into non-bank businesses and real estate, so that depositors' money supports banking rather than unrelated ventures. It caps holdings in a single insurer and in any other single non-bank business, all non-bank equity together, and real estate.
Treasury and finance check every proposed equity investment against all the limits before it reaches the board, using total capital as defined in the directive.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/92/2024, Limits on bank investments
regulation.text: In force from 19 July 2024 (repealing SBB/65/2017): limits of 5% for a single insurer and 10% for any other single non-bank business, 15% of total capital for all non-bank equity investments together, and 10% for real estate. A bank may own up to 100% of a capital market service provider with NBE approval.

worked.title: Bank A aggregate equity limit check (Birr millions)

rows.label: Proposed stake in an insurance company
Real estate limit: 10% of total capital

worked.note: The aggregate limit is met with little headroom; the single-insurer limit must also be checked against the base the directive uses.

scenario.title: An investment bank subsidiary
scenario.situation: Bank A's board wants to set up a wholly owned investment bank to act on the Ethiopian Securities Exchange. Finance notes that 100% ownership would far exceed the 10% single non-bank business limit.
scenario.question: What is the correct position?
options: It is not allowed under any condition
SBB/92/2024 allows up to 100% ownership of a capital market service provider with NBE approval
It is allowed without any approval
scenario.explain: The directive makes a specific exception for capital market service providers, subject to NBE approval.

lessons.title: Matched-maturity funds transfer pricing
body: Funds transfer pricing (FTP) charges lending units for the funds they use and credits deposit units for the funds they bring, at internal rates set by treasury. With matched-maturity FTP, each product is priced off a curve at the tenor of its cash flows or repricing, so interest rate and liquidity risk move to treasury and the business units keep only their commercial margin.

The FTP curve starts from market rates (interbank, T-bill and bond yields) and adds a liquidity premium that grows with tenor, reflecting the cost of term funding in a market where most deposits are short. A loan price then adds expected credit loss, operating cost and a charge for the capital it uses.

visual.caption: Treasury owns the first two parts; the business unit owns the rest.

worked.title: Pricing a 3-year loan to Hawassa Textile PLC (course figures)

rows.label: FTP base rate, 3-year point of the curve
Capital charge: 11% capital x (25% target return minus 16% funds cost)

worked.note: A rate below 20% would win the deal but destroy value; any discount needs ALCO approval with a reason.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest rates (as amended)
regulation.text: Lending rates are set by each bank on board-approved written criteria. An FTP-based pricing model is a practical way to make those criteria explicit and consistent, and to report weighted average rates to the NBE within the required 7 working days of month end.

lessons.title: Using FTP for products and branch profitability
body: Without FTP, a branch that collects deposits but lends little looks unprofitable, and a branch that lends heavily looks brilliant, even if it is funded by the first one. FTP credits deposit gatherers for the value of their funds and charges lenders for theirs, so both see their true contribution.
FTP also steers behavior. Raising the credit for long time deposits encourages branches to sell them; raising the liquidity charge on long fixed-rate loans makes lenders price the risk they create.

worked.title: Bank A Merkato branch contribution with FTP (Birr millions, one year)

rows.label: Deposits Birr 2,000 million: FTP credit 13% minus customer cost 8%
Loans Birr 800 million: customer rate 18% minus FTP charge 15.5%

worked.note: Most of the branch's value comes from cheap deposits. Without FTP it would have looked like a weak lending branch.

scenario.title: A branch manager objects
scenario.situation: The manager of Bank A's Bole branch, Rahel Getachew, complains that the FTP charge of 15.5% on her loans is unfair because the bank's average deposit cost is only 9%. She wants loans charged at 9%.
scenario.question: How should treasury respond?
options: Agree: use the average cost of deposits for all loans
Explain that the FTP charge reflects the market cost of matched funding and liquidity at the loan's tenor; cheap deposits are credited to the branches that raise them
Remove FTP for her branch only
Charge her loans at the NBE standing lending rate
scenario.explain: Average cost pricing hides rate and liquidity risk and rewards lenders with other branches' deposits. Matched-maturity FTP prices funds at their market value and credits deposit gatherers.

example.title: Steering branches with FTP
example.text: After the 30-day funding gap appeared, Bank A raised the FTP credit for 6 to 12 month time deposits by 1 point. Within two months branches had sold Birr 2.4 billion of such deposits, lengthening funding without a public rate war.

takeaways: The portfolio is a liquidity buffer, an income source and repo collateral; Birr sovereign exposures carry a 0% risk weight but still carry rate risk.
T-bill price = face / (1 + yield x days / 365); a discount rate is lower than the yield on the same bill.
IFRS 9 classification follows the business model; a liquidity buffer usually fits FVOCI.
SBB/92/2024 caps all non-bank equity at 15% of total capital and real estate at 10%, with an exception for capital market subsidiaries with NBE approval.
Matched-maturity FTP moves rate and liquidity risk to treasury and shows the true contribution of products and branches.

quiz.q: What is the price per Birr 100 of a 182-day T-bill at a 12% yield (actual/365)?
For the same bill, which is higher?
quiz.explain: The yield is computed on the lower price paid, so it is always above the discount rate.

quiz.q: Bank A's total capital is Birr 12.5 billion. What is its aggregate limit for non-bank equity under SBB/92/2024?
quiz.explain: 15% x Birr 12.5 billion = Birr 1.875 billion.

quiz.q: A securities book held to collect and to sell when liquidity is needed is usually measured at:
quiz.explain: The collect-and-sell business model points to FVOCI under IFRS 9.

quiz.q: Under matched-maturity FTP, who bears the interest rate risk of a fixed-rate loan?
options: The branch that made the loan
quiz.explain: FTP locks the branch's funding cost at origination, so treasury carries and manages the rate risk.

quiz.q: Why does an FTP curve include a liquidity premium that rises with tenor?
options: Because term funding is scarcer and costlier than short deposits
quiz.explain: Long assets funded by short deposits create liquidity risk; the premium prices it.

modules.title: Market risk governance and the capstone ALCO
modules.summary: Set and monitor treasury limits, report as an independent middle office, and write and defend Bank A's ALCO paper.
objectives: Design a treasury limits framework that links to board risk appetite
Prepare middle office reports and escalate breaches
Recognize model risk in ALM and VaR assumptions
Structure an ALCO paper with clear decisions
Recommend pricing, investment and funding actions for Bank A

lessons.title: The limits framework
body: Limits turn the board's risk appetite into numbers dealers and ALM can act on. Regulatory limits, such as the 18% open position cap, are the outer wall; internal limits sit inside them so that a normal day never touches the wall.

A complete framework covers FX positions overall and per currency, dealer and overnight limits, stop-loss limits, interbank counterparty limits, earnings at risk and EVE, liquidity ratios and survival horizon, and investment portfolio duration.

items.label: FX position
items.text: Internal overall limit below 18% of Tier 1, plus per-currency limits

items.label: Dealer limits
items.text: Intraday and overnight per dealer

items.label: Stop-loss
items.text: Loss level that forces position reduction

items.label: Counterparty
items.text: Interbank and forward exposure per bank and client

items.label: EaR and EVE
items.text: Share of NII and of equity for a set shock

items.label: Liquidity
items.text: Liquid asset ratio buffer and survival horizon

regulation.source: NBE Risk Management Guidelines (May 2010) and Directive No. SBB/96/2025
regulation.text: The guidelines expect board-approved limits for market and liquidity risk, monitored by an independent risk function and reviewed by the ALCO. SBB/96/2025 sets the regulatory outer limit for FX: an overall open position within plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 capital at each close.

scenario.title: Setting the internal FX limit
scenario.situation: Bank A's regulatory cap is 18% of Tier 1. Daily swings in customer flows move the position by up to 3% of Tier 1 between morning and close.
scenario.question: Where should the ALCO set the internal overall limit?
options: At 25%, since breaches can be squared next day
At about 15%, leaving room for normal swings before the close
scenario.explain: An internal limit below the cap by at least the normal daily swing keeps the bank compliant at close. Setting it at the cap guarantees occasional breaches.

lessons.title: Middle office reporting and escalation
body: The middle office is independent of the dealers and reports to risk. Each day it revalues positions at market rates, computes profit and loss, checks every limit and sends a short report to the treasurer and CRO. Breaches are escalated the same day, with the cause and the plan to fix them.
A good daily report fits on one page: positions against limits, utilization in percent, breaches, large deals and any items needing a decision.

worked.title: Bank A daily limit report (extract)

rows.label: Overall FX position: 20.1% of Tier 1 against internal 15%

worked.note: Three breaches and two near-limits: this is the agenda for an extraordinary ALCO, not a routine report.

items.label: Revalue
items.text: Positions at closing market rates

items.label: Check limits
items.text: Every limit, every day

items.label: Report
items.text: One page to treasurer and CRO

items.label: Escalate
items.text: Breaches same day, with cause and fix

items.label: Follow up
items.text: Confirm the breach is closed

example.title: The report that was ignored
example.text: At a bank in Dire Dawa, the middle office reported a growing short dollar position for three weeks, but the reports went only to the treasurer, who ran the position. When the birr moved sharply, the loss was large. The bank then sent all limit reports directly to the CRO as well.

lessons.title: Model risk in ALM
body: Every ALM number depends on assumptions: how much savings reprices, how many time deposits roll over, what volatility to use, how fast loans prepay. When an assumption is wrong, the model is precise and wrong at the same time.

Control model risk by documenting every assumption with its evidence, back-testing results against what actually happened, having someone independent review the models, and showing the ALCO how sensitive the results are to the key assumptions.
points: Back-test VaR: count days when actual losses exceeded VaR
Back-test deposit assumptions against real outflows each quarter
Show sensitivity: EaR with 30 billion and with 40 billion of repricing savings
Review models after any regime change, such as the July 2024 float

scenario.title: Too many VaR exceptions
scenario.situation: Over the last 100 trading days Bank A's 95% one-day VaR was exceeded on 14 days. At 95% confidence you would expect about 5.
scenario.question: What does this tell the ALCO?
options: The model understates risk; review the volatility inputs and tighten limits until it is fixed
scenario.explain: Nearly three times the expected exceptions means the model underestimates losses. Fix the inputs and rely more on stress limits meanwhile; VaR stays useful once recalibrated.

example.title: Sensitivity on one page
example.text: Dawit showed the ALCO that EaR for a 2 point rise ranged from minus 4.7% of NII if 30 billion of savings repriced to about minus 7% if 40 billion did. The committee saw that its limit was only safe under the more optimistic assumption, and asked for six months of new evidence.

lessons.title: Writing the ALCO paper
body: An ALCO paper is a decision document, not a data dump. It opens with the decisions requested, then shows the evidence, the options considered and the risks of each. Supporting tables go in an annex.

In the classroom version of this course, the ALCO paper carries 40% of the grade, the test 30%, a gap analysis of your own bank from public data 20%, and participation 10%. The online capstone below follows the same structure.

items.label: Decisions requested
items.text: Three to five, each one sentence

items.label: Position today
items.text: Liquidity, rate, FX and capital against limits

items.label: Outlook
items.text: Latest MPC decision, rates, inflation, FX flows

items.label: Options and impacts
items.text: Each option with its effect on the limits

items.label: Recommendation
items.text: What, who, by when, and how it will be monitored

lessons.tip: If the ALCO chair reads only the first half page, the decisions must still be clear.

lessons.title: Capstone part 1: diagnosing Bank A
body: Bring together the analysis from Modules 1 to 4. Bank A has a 30-day funding gap of Birr 5 billion and a course-basis LCR of 93%. Its short dollar position is 20.1% of Tier 1, above the 18% cap. Its loan-to-deposit ratio of about 86% is high enough to attract a targeted reserve requirement, and a 2 point rate rise would cut net interest income by about 4.7% and economic value by about 13%.

The issues are linked. Loan growth ahead of deposits caused the funding gap and the high ratio; import demand ahead of FX inflows caused the short position; short deposits against longer loans caused the rate exposure. The solutions must be linked too.

worked.title: Bank A ALCO dashboard
worked.note: Liquidity and FX need action this week; rate risk and loan growth need a three-month plan.

scenario.title: The first decision
scenario.situation: The ALCO has time for only one decision today. The FX position is above the regulatory cap at close, the survival horizon is 2 days below minimum, and the EaR is inside its limit.
scenario.question: Which item comes first?
options: Square the FX position within the regulatory cap by the next business day and report, while treasury begins the liquidity actions under the CFP
scenario.explain: A regulatory breach has a fixed deadline, so it comes first. Liquidity actions start in parallel under the existing plan; EaR is within limit and can wait for the next meeting.

lessons.title: Capstone part 2: pricing, investments and funding
body: Now recommend. Pricing: raise FTP credits and customer rates for 6 to 12 month time deposits to lengthen funding, and lift the liquidity premium on long fixed-rate loans. Investments: stop buying long bonds, keep T-bills short and in an FVOCI liquidity book, and prepare repo documents. Funding: repo T-bills for the immediate gap, grow term deposits for the structural gap and slow loan commitments until the loan-to-deposit ratio falls.

FX: buy dollars to bring the position within an internal limit of about 15%, offer forwards to exporters such as Sidama Coffee Exporters PLC to secure future dollar inflows, and price import sales to cover the cost of cover. Each recommendation should state its effect on the dashboard.

left.title: This week
items: Buy about USD 1.6 million or more to square the FX breach
Repo Birr 3 billion of T-bills
Report the breach to the NBE
Pause new long fixed-rate loan offers

right.title: Next three months
items: Raise 6 to 12 month deposits by Birr 5 billion
Bring internal FX position to 15% or less
Set loan growth to funded deposit growth
Re-test EaR, EVE and LCR monthly

scenario.title: Pricing the deposit campaign
scenario.situation: Competitors pay about 14% for 12-month deposits. Bank A's matched FTP credit at 12 months is 15%. Treasury proposes a 14.5% customer rate for a Birr 5 billion campaign.
scenario.question: Is the proposal sound?
options: No: any rate above competitors is wasteful
No: deposits should be priced at the NBE standing deposit rate
Yes, but only if the rate is above the National Bank Rate
Yes: it lengthens funding, the rate stays below the FTP credit so branches earn a margin, and the cost is below NBE standing lending at 19%
scenario.explain: The campaign fixes the structural gap at a cost below both the FTP value of 12-month funds and the NBE backstop. Being slightly above competitors is the price of attracting term funds.

example.title: The ALCO decides
example.text: Bank A's ALCO, chaired by the CEO, approved four actions: square the FX position the next day, repo Birr 3 billion of T-bills, launch a Birr 5 billion 12-month deposit campaign at 14.5%, and cap new loan commitments at the level of new deposits for one quarter. Meron Assefa, the CFO, will report progress on the dashboard at every meeting until all indicators are back within limits.

takeaways: Internal limits sit inside regulatory limits by at least the normal daily swing, so the bank stays compliant at close.
The middle office revalues, checks every limit and escalates breaches to the treasurer and the CRO the same day.
ALM models are only as good as their assumptions; document, back-test and show sensitivity.
An ALCO paper starts with the decisions requested and shows the effect of each option on the limits.
For Bank A, square the FX breach first, then fix liquidity, then lengthen funding and align loan growth with deposits.

quiz.q: Why should an internal FX limit sit below the 18% regulatory cap?
options: So that normal daily swings do not cause a breach at close
quiz.explain: A buffer equal to the normal swing keeps the closing position within the cap.

quiz.q: To whom should the middle office send limit breach reports, as a minimum?
options: The treasurer and the chief risk officer
quiz.explain: Reporting to risk as well as treasury keeps the check independent of the position taker.

quiz.q: A 95% one-day VaR is exceeded on 14 of 100 days. What is the expected number of exceptions?
quiz.explain: At 95% confidence, about 5% of days, or 5 of 100, should exceed VaR.

quiz.q: What should come first in an ALCO paper?
quiz.explain: A decision document leads with the decisions; evidence and tables follow.

quiz.q: Which Bank A issue has a fixed regulatory deadline?
options: The FX position above 18% of Tier 1
quiz.explain: SBB/96/2025 requires the excess to be squared by the next business day.

quiz.q: Why does a 14.5% 12-month deposit campaign make sense for Bank A?
options: It is the highest rate in the market
It lengthens funding at a cost below the 15% FTP credit and the 19% NBE standing lending rate
The NBE sets 14.5% as the minimum
quiz.explain: Term deposits close the structural gap more cheaply than the alternatives.

exam.q: Bank A's 0 to 3 month gap is minus Birr 20 billion (midpoint 1.5 months). Roughly how much does NII change in the next 12 months for a 1 point rise from that bucket?
exam.explain: Minus 20 billion x 1% x 10.5 / 12 = minus Birr 175 million.

exam.q: Assets of Birr 120 billion have modified duration 1.0 and liabilities of Birr 108 billion have modified duration 0.5. What is the change in EVE for a 2 point rise?
exam.explain: Minus (120 x 1.0 minus 108 x 0.5) x 2% = minus 66 x 2% = minus Birr 1.32 billion.

exam.q: Which statement about customer rates after NBE/INT/13/2026 is correct?
options: Lending rates may not exceed the National Bank Rate plus 3 points
The NBE approves each bank's rates in advance
Banks set rates freely on written board-approved criteria and report changes within 5 working days
exam.explain: The directive removed the minimum deposit rate and requires board approval and NBE reporting.

exam.q: After MPC No. 7, what did the NBE introduce in place of the credit growth cap?
options: A targeted (additional) reserve requirement linked to a bank's loan-to-deposit ratio
A ban on new loans above 80% of deposits
exam.explain: The targeted reserve requirement may be imposed on individual banks based on their loan-to-deposit ratio.

exam.q: A bank's savings deposits are Birr 48 billion. Its data show that only Birr 30 billion repriced with past policy changes. In the repricing gap, the 0 to 3 month bucket should hold:
options: Birr 30 billion, documented as an ALCO-approved behavioral assumption
Nothing, since savings have no maturity
exam.explain: Non-maturity deposits are placed by evidence-based behavioral assumptions approved and reviewed by the ALCO.

exam.q: Bank A's 30-day inflows are Birr 8 billion and outflows Birr 11.5 billion. Liquid assets after haircuts are Birr 2.8 billion. What should treasury conclude?
options: The net gap of Birr 3.5 billion exceeds the buffer by Birr 0.7 billion, so funding must be arranged now
exam.explain: 8 minus 11.5 = minus 3.5; the buffer of 2.8 leaves a Birr 0.7 billion shortfall.

exam.q: HQLA are Birr 12 billion, stressed outflows Birr 16 billion and inflows Birr 4 billion. What is the LCR on a course basis?
Which funding action belongs at the end of a contingency funding plan?
options: NBE lender of last resort support at a rate above the policy rate
exam.explain: Lender of last resort support is the costly final step after market options.

exam.q: Bank A's Tier 1 capital rises to Birr 12 billion. Its overall short position is Birr 2.3 billion. By how much must it reduce the position by the next business day?
exam.explain: The cap is 18% x 12 billion = 2.16 billion; 2.3 minus 2.16 = Birr 140 million.

exam.q: A bank is long EUR worth Birr 400 million and short USD worth Birr 1,500 million and GBP worth Birr 200 million. Using the shorthand method, what is the overall position?
exam.explain: Total shorts are 1,700 and total longs 400; the shorthand method takes the larger, 1,700.

exam.q: USD/ETB is 152.00 / 154.00 and EUR/USD is 1.0700 / 1.0730. What is the bank's EUR/ETB buying rate?
exam.explain: The bank buys at bid times bid: 152.00 x 1.0700 = 162.64.

exam.q: Spot USD/ETB is 150.00. The 180-day Birr rate is 14% and the USD rate is 4% (actual/365). What is the forward mid rate, roughly?
A position of Birr 1,000 million has a daily volatility of 0.8%. What is the 95% one-day VaR?
Bank A's paid-up capital is Birr 6 billion and it holds foreign cash notes worth Birr 790 million. Under FXD/01/2024, how much must it hand to the NBE?
exam.explain: Notes above 10% of paid-up capital (Birr 600 million) go to the NBE: 790 minus 600 = Birr 190 million.

exam.q: A goods exporter receives USD 1 million after MPC No. 7. What share must it surrender for conversion, and what may it retain?
exam.explain: MPC No. 7 cut the surrender requirement on goods exports to 30%; service exporters may retain 100% under FXD/04/2026.

exam.q: A 91-day T-bill is priced at 97.50 per 100. What is its yield (actual/365)?
Interbank funding costs 14.6% and a 364-day T-bill yields 12%. What is the main risk of buying the bill with overnight funding?
options: No risk, since the bill has 0% risk weight
Negative carry and added rate and liquidity risk
exam.explain: Funding above the asset yield loses money each day, and a long bill adds duration while the bank needs liquidity.

exam.q: Total capital is Birr 10 billion. Existing non-bank equity is Birr 1.2 billion. What is the largest additional non-bank equity investment SBB/92/2024's aggregate limit allows?
exam.explain: The aggregate limit is 15% x 10 billion = 1.5 billion; 1.5 minus 1.2 = Birr 300 million, subject also to the single-investment limits.

exam.q: FTP base rate is 14.5%, liquidity premium 0.8%, credit spread 2%, operating cost 1.2% and capital charge 1%. What is the minimum loan rate?
Bank A must choose one action today: FX position above the 18% cap, survival horizon 28 days against 30, EaR within limit. What is the right sequence?
options: Reprice loans, then deal with FX
Square FX by the next business day and report, start CFP liquidity actions in parallel, review rate risk at the next ALCO
Wait for the next MPC meeting
Raise all deposit rates and ignore FX
exam.explain: The regulatory breach has a fixed deadline, liquidity follows the existing plan, and in-limit rate risk can wait.
